models.label: eurollm-9b
models.notes: Model card YAML front matter declares license: apache-2.0. Base model (utter-project/EuroLLM-9B) also carries apache-2.0 — no license conflict between base and instruct fine-tune. No separate LICENSE file found in the repo tree (404), but the HF metadata tag is authoritative. Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved and permits commercial use. No additional use-restriction overlays or community-license terms were found. Developed under EU funding by Unbabel, IST, University of Edinburgh et al.

models.label: gemma-3-4b
models.notes: HF model card YAML declares 'license: gemma'. License is the Gemma Terms of Use — a custom Google license, not OSI-approved. Requires mandatory acceptance before accessing weights (gated model). Includes an incorporated Prohibited Use Policy and distribution requirements that go beyond OSI-permissive licenses. Commercial use is permitted but the acceptable-use clause and Google's reserved right to restrict usage mean this does not qualify as OSI-permissive. Note: Gemma 4 later switched to Apache-2.0, but Gemma 3 (including gemma-3-4b-it) remains under Gemma Terms of Use.

models.label: gemma-4-e4b
models.notes: HF model card YAML declares 'apache-2.0' but the mandatory license_link (https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/gemma_4_license) is a Gemma-specific document that supplements Apache 2.0 with binding Gemma Terms of Use and a Prohibited Use Policy. Users must comply with the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy and pass those restrictions downstream — obligations not present in standard Apache 2.0. This is the same hybrid pattern used by all Gemma generations and is NOT OSI-compliant Apache 2.0. Classified as open-weight-non-osi (custom Google Gemma Terms). Note: a GGUF quantized variant exists at google/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf but is not needed for this matrix entry.

models.label: granite-3.3-8b
models.notes: YAML front-matter `license: apache-2.0` and model card body both declare Apache 2.0 explicitly (link to https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0). Consistent with the entire IBM Granite 3.x/4.x family, all released under Apache 2.0. No custom community license or use restrictions observed.

models.label: granite-4.1-3b
models.notes: Model card YAML front-matter declares 'license: apache-2.0' and links to https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0. Released 2026-04-29. Instruction-tuned from granite-4.1-3b-base, which also carries Apache 2.0 (IBM Granite models have been consistently Apache-2.0 since Granite 3.x). No custom addendum or use restrictions found. Fully OSI-permissive.

models.label: hermes-3-8b
models.notes: Model card YAML front matter and HF API both declare license: llama3. This is a finetune of meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B; base model license governs. The Llama 3.1 Community License is not OSI-approved: it contains a >700M MAU commercial gate requiring Meta approval, plus an Acceptable Use Policy. Not OSI-permissive; classified open-weight-non-osi.

models.label: llama-3.2-3b
models.notes: HF model card YAML front matter: 'license: llama3.2'. LICENSE.txt title: 'LLAMA 3.2 COMMUNITY LICENSE AGREEMENT' (effective 2024-09-25). Both sources agree. This is Meta's custom community license — NOT OSI-approved: it requires attribution ('Built with Llama'), mandates 'Llama' in derivative names, restricts commercial use for products with >700M MAU without explicit Meta approval, and includes a mandatory Acceptable Use Policy. licenseClass = open-weight-non-osi; allowedInDefaultMatrix = false.

models.label: ministral-3-14b
models.notes: Model card YAML front-matter declares 'apache-2.0'; the card body also links to apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt and explicitly states commercial use is permitted. Apache 2.0 is fully OSI-approved permissive — no MAU caps, no acceptable-use riders.

models.label: mistral-nemo-12b
models.notes: Model card YAML front matter states `license: apache-2.0`; body text confirms 'Released under the Apache 2 License'. Official Mistral AI announcement (mistral.ai/news/mistral-nemo/) also confirms Apache 2.0 for both base and instruct checkpoints. No separate LICENSE file exists in the HF repo (returns 404) — the metadata tag and official announcement are the authoritative sources and fully agree. This is a 12B instruct model jointly developed by Mistral AI and NVIDIA. Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved permissive; no usage restrictions beyond attribution.

models.label: phi-4-14b
models.notes: Model card YAML front-matter declares 'license: mit' and the raw LICENSE file at the repo root is a standard MIT License (copyright Microsoft Corporation). Both sources agree — no custom restrictions, no acceptable-use policy overlay. Fully OSI-permissive.

models.label: phi-4-mini

models.label: qwen3-4b-instruct

The -2507 suffix is a date-stamped update release of Qwen3-4B-Instruct and inherits the same Apache-2.0 terms.

models.label: qwen3-8b
models.notes: Model card YAML license tag and the LICENSE file both declare Apache-2.0 (copyright Alibaba Cloud 2024). Standard OSI-permissive terms — no commercial restrictions, no acceptable-use policy, no MAU cap. Fully permissive for RAG-eval use.

models.label: qwen3.5-27b

models.label: qwen3.5-2b

models.label: qwen3.5-4b

models.label: qwen3.5-9b

Both sources agree — no custom Qwen license, no use restrictions beyond standard Apache-2.0 attribution/patent terms. OSI-permissive, allowed in default matrix.

models.label: smollm3-3b
models.notes: Model card YAML front-matter declares 'apache-2.0'; body section also links to https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0. No separate LICENSE file in the repo (not present — HF metadata is the authoritative declaration). Base model HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-Base also declares apache-2.0. All sources are consistent. Model is described as 'fully open' (training data, datasets, and intermediate checkpoints publicly available). Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved and imposes no commercial or MAU restrictions.

models.label: arctic-l-v2
models.notes: Apache-2.0 confirmed by three independent sources: HuggingFace model card YAML front matter (license: apache-2.0), raw README.md header, and the upstream Snowflake-Labs/arctic-embed GitHub repo LICENSE file + footer stating 'Arctic is licensed under the Apache-2'. Docs explicitly state models can be used for commercial purposes free of charge. No disagreement between model card and upstream repo.

models.label: bge-m3
models.notes: MIT license declared in README.md YAML front matter (`license: mit`) and confirmed by HuggingFace API (`cardData.license: mit`, tags include `license:mit`). No separate LICENSE file exists in the repo — only the model card metadata carries the declaration, but all three sources (model card page, raw README.md, HF API) agree. MIT is OSI-permissive; no use restrictions.

models.label: cand-gte-base
models.notes: License is unambiguously Apache-2.0 per model card YAML front matter (confirmed via raw README.md and HF API). No LICENSE file at repo root (404) but model card is authoritative and consistent. GGUF is NOT available: the model uses an encoder-only (BERT/new_model) architecture that llama.cpp does not support for conversion — HF discussion #18 confirms 'ERROR:hf-to-gguf:Model NewModel is not supported'. The only GTE GGUF on HF is gpustack/gte-multilingual-reranker-base-GGUF (the reranker variant, different model). Because no usable GGUF exists, allowedInDefaultMatrix is false despite the permissive license.

models.label: cand-mxbai-embed
models.notes: License confirmed Apache-2.0 from both HF model card YAML metadata and the LICENSE file (Copyright 2024 mixedbread ai inc.) — no conflict. The official repo (mixedbread-ai/mxbai-embed-large-v1) ships only an F16 GGUF (mxbai-embed-large-v1-f16.gguf, 670 MB) in its /gguf subfolder. ChristianAzinn/mxbai-embed-large-v1-gguf provides Q4_K_M (216 MB) and Q8_0 (358 MB) quantizations converted with llama.cpp. Model is BERT-large sized (~0.3B params), trained with Matryoshka Representation Learning; not a finetune of a restricted base model.

models.label: e5-base
models.notes: MIT license confirmed via HF API metadata tag (license:mit); no separate LICENSE file in the repo root (404), normal for HF-hosted models declaring license in card front-matter only. License is fine, but EXCLUDED from the default pack on 2026-06-14 for a TECHNICAL reason: the cstr/multilingual-e5-base-GGUF Q8_0 declares model architecture 'xlmr', which node-llama-cpp 3.18.1 (llama.cpp b8390) cannot load ('unknown model architecture: xlmr'). Its sibling multilingual-e5-large loads only because that GGUF declares 'bert'. Re-add once a 'bert'-arch multilingual-e5-base GGUF is found and load-tested. Model supports 100+ languages with 768-dim embeddings (mean-pool).

models.label: embeddinggemma
models.notes: Model card frontmatter declares `license: gemma`. The Gemma Terms of Use (https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms) is a custom Google proprietary agreement — NOT an OSI-approved license. Commercial use is allowed but distribution requires passing on the same restrictions and complying with the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy. This is the same license class as other Gemma models (Gemma 1–3 and variants); Gemma 4 is Apache-2.0, but embeddinggemma-300m is not Gemma 4. Not permissive by OSI standards.

models.label: granite-emb
models.notes: HuggingFace model card YAML declares 'license: apache-2.0'. GitHub repo ibm-granite/granite-embedding-models confirms Apache 2.0 with an explicit LICENSE file and states models are 'offered under the Apache 2.0 license for both research and commercial innovation'. IBM's own Watsonx documentation corroborates this. All sources agree — no conflict. 278M-parameter multilingual embedding model supporting 12 languages.

models.label: e5-large
models.notes: License declared as 'mit' in the model card YAML front matter and confirmed via the HuggingFace API (cardData). No separate LICENSE file exists in the repository (404). MIT is a true OSI-permissive license with no commercial restrictions. Model is a multilingual text embedding model (560M params, 1024-dim) trained by intfloat/Microsoft Research.

models.label: nomic-v2
models.notes: License declared as apache-2.0 in model card YAML front-matter; no separate LICENSE file found in repo (404), so YAML metadata is the authoritative source. Both README fetches independently confirmed apache-2.0. Model is described as fully open-source (weights + code + training data). Official GGUF repo (nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v2-moe-GGUF) is published by nomic-ai themselves and contains Q4_K_M (344 MB) and Q8_0 (512 MB) among 17 quantization variants. MoE multilingual embedding model supporting ~100 languages, trained on 1.6B pairs with Matryoshka support (768→256 dims).

models.label: qwen3-emb-0.6b
models.notes: YAML front-matter in README.md (raw/main/README.md) declares `license: apache-2.0` verbatim. Web search across HF and Qwen blog confirms Apache-2.0. No separate LICENSE file is served at the repo root (404), but the README front-matter is the canonical HuggingFace license declaration. Apache-2.0 is a true OSI-approved permissive license with no commercial restrictions. This is a first-party Qwen release (Alibaba), not a finetune, so no base-model license inheritance issue.

models.label: qwen3-emb-4b
models.notes: Model card YAML front-matter declares 'license: apache-2.0'. No separate LICENSE file exists in the repo (directory listing confirmed). README body adds no additional restrictions or custom Qwen addenda. All Qwen3 dense models including this 4B embedding variant are released under plain Apache-2.0 by Alibaba Cloud. OSI-permissive, no usage restrictions beyond standard Apache-2.0 attribution.

models.label: mistral-small-3.2-24b
models.notes: License declared as 'apache-2.0' in the YAML front matter of the model card README.md. No separate LICENSE file exists in the repo (returns 404). This is consistent with Mistral AI's prior Small 3.x releases which are all Apache-2.0. Apache-2.0 is a genuine OSI-approved permissive license — no commercial-use restrictions, no acceptable-use policy addendum. Confirmed via raw README.md fetch and web search cross-check.

models.label: bge-reranker-base
models.notes: License: model card YAML declares 'mit'; README body confirms 'FlagEmbedding is licensed under the MIT License ... commercial use free of charge'; no separate LICENSE file in repo but card metadata and body agree. GGUF: only F16 (564 MB) confirmed in sinjab/bge-reranker-base-F16-GGUF via HF API — Q4_K_M/Q8_0 mentioned in the sinjab/gguf-rerankers GitHub README but those files do not appear in the actual HF repo. llama.cpp rankAll: PR #9510 added LLAMA_POOLING_TYPE_RANK for cross-encoder rerankers, tested against XLMRoberta-based models (bge-reranker-v2-m3, jina-reranker). bge-reranker-base is BERT-based (BertForSequenceClassification), a different architecture from the officially tested XLMRoberta models; mainline llama.cpp rankAll support for vanilla BERT cross-encoders is not confirmed — use with caution or prefer v2-m3 for llama.cpp.

models.label: bge-reranker-v2-m3
models.notes: Model card YAML front matter declares 'license: apache-2.0'; confirmed via raw README.md fetch. No separate LICENSE file found in the repo root (404), but the YAML metadata is the authoritative HF declaration. Base model is BAAI/bge-m3 (MIT), which is also OSI-permissive — no license inheritance concern. Other variants in the v2 family (bge-reranker-v2-gemma, bge-reranker-v2-minicpm-layerwise) use Gemma/MiniCPM backbones with non-OSI terms, but v2-m3 is clean.

models.label: cand-gte-reranker
models.notes: License confirmed as apache-2.0 from both HF API cardData.license field and model card YAML frontmatter — fully OSI-permissive, no usage restrictions. Standalone encoder-only model (306M params, 8192 token context, 70+ languages), not a finetune, so no base-model license inheritance concern. GGUF exists at gpustack/gte-multilingual-reranker-base-GGUF with Q4_K_M (235 MB) and Q8_0 (332 MB). CRITICAL CAVEAT: the GGUF was 'patched by llama-box' (gpustack/llama-box fork) and the README explicitly states 'Experimental supported by gpustack/llama-box v0.0.72+ only' — it references a specific llama.cpp commit (f4d2b88). Mainline llama.cpp supports cross-encoder reranking via --pooling rank, but confirmed working models are BGE/Jina/MS MARCO families; gte-multilingual-reranker-base is NOT on the confirmed mainline rankAll list. May require llama-box or a patched llama.cpp build rather than stock mainline llama.cpp for rankAll.

models.label: cand-mxbai-rerank
models.notes: License: Apache 2.0 confirmed in model card YAML front matter (license: apache-2.0) — truly OSI-permissive, no use restrictions. Architecture: Qwen2 (Qwen2ForCausalLM), 0.5B params, fine-tuned as a cross-encoder reranker via GRPO + contrastive + preference learning. GGUF exists at mradermacher/mxbai-rerank-base-v2-GGUF (Q4_K_M=398MB, Q8_0=531MB). CRITICAL: llama.cpp mainline reranking (rankAll/--reranking) is BROKEN for mxbai rerankers as of October 2025 — open bug #16407 (ggml-org/llama.cpp) documents that mxbai rerankers produce near-zero or incorrect relevance scores in llama-server; only Jina-reranker-v2 partially works. Because the GGUF cannot be reliably used with mainline llama.cpp rankAll, allowedInDefaultMatrix is set to false despite the OSI-permissive license.

models.label: jina-reranker-v2
models.notes: Model card YAML front matter explicitly sets license: cc-by-nc-4.0. The card text states it is 'licenced for research and evaluation purposes under CC-BY-NC-4.0'; commercial use requires Jina AI's hosted Reranker API, AWS SageMaker, or Azure Marketplace. Not OSI-permissive — excluded from the default matrix.
